findings.text: the method note says the typed-reissued window returns "exactly 5 rows / 93 names", but the same document's row 1 (:34), its own log (diag.log:206-207) and the plan's landing comment (docs/plans/paid-identity-deletion-protection.html:929) all read 93 rows / 93 distinct names, every dated-window query in the receipts returns 0 or 93 (main.log:116-140), and the nearest five-row figures are an unrelated phase breakdown (spend.log:302-304) and an operation census (main.log:361-363), so the paragraph written to teach the next node the typed-bound recipe carries a count that nothing measured; the same sentence stands at docs/evidence/archive/paid-identity-deletion-protection-landed.html:58.

the gloss reads the plan's "protects 75 of 93" as "the count that did *not* pay", inverting the plan's own §2 definition (docs/plans/paid-identity-deletion-protection.html:184-187, where "did it cost money?" protects 75 of 93 and misses 18 all with zero recorded spend), so a reader following the label compares a non-paying count against the paying count the row actually measured and the plan's central spend criterion reads backwards in the audit of it.

the six query logs and the audit scripts that are the primary receipt for all sixteen rows live only under /tmp/pidp-audit with no retained copy, digest, or reproduction recipe beside the committed documents, and the lists have already drifted - :57 names audit_discovery.py, which does not exist on disk, the present audit_queries.py is named by no document, and the three documents carry three different log sets (plan-figure-audit.md:171-181, the archive :69-71) - so the evidence chain cannot be repaired from the record once the scratch allocation is cleared.

the largest remaining block (§7a stages 2-4, priced 4-6 worker-hours) rests on "a 34-file reader census" that appears in no receipt: the only recorder of that census is a bare count of 75 with no command and no match list (code-read.log:18-19), the standalone figure 34 occurs nowhere in the logs (the only other 34 is an unrelated operation's names count, main.log:232), and no retained script contains the extraction - so the census that classifies the first unstarted beat (:129) and prices the sprint's remaining work can be re-derived only by inventing the aperture.

justifications.durability: the re-measurement survives as committed documents but arms no test and no recurring measurement, so the drift it measured (ledger sums understated by 23-40%, plan-figure-audit.md:25-28) will silently return by the plan's next read.
justifications.evidence: every done-when element is recorded and the three audit-doc gates pass on this review's own re-run at exit 0 (plan-figure-audit.md:18-23, :32-49, :123-152), but four verified receipt defects cost five points: the typed-window count at :165 contradicts the node's own row 1 (:34) and log (diag.log:206-207), the row-3 gloss at :36 inverts the plan's §2 definition (plan :184-187), the primary receipts exist only on the /tmp scratch allocation with the three documents carrying three different receipt lists, and the reader census behind the first-unstarted-beat call and its 4-6 h price (:129, :146) retains no reproducible extraction.
justifications.fit: the three documents follow the repository's evidence-doc idiom with no plan label or version suffix in any path or comment, and the single blemish is the commit subject of 959e5d29 reading "line graph" where "live graph" was meant (self-recorded in the source run's manifest.md:9).
